note: Mozambique's largest banks are Millennium bim, BCI and Standard Bank Moçambique; Millennium bim's price lists were read, and BCI's current price list couldn't be found (its latest complete list that turned up is dated 30 June 2025 and a card leaflet from a campaign that ended in March 2025, neither current), nor could Standard Bank's. Millennium bim's simplified price list (in force from 22 May 2026) gives its Classic credit card a first annual fee of 800 meticais and 36% a year, 3% a month; its complete price list (in force from 15 January 2026; the latest complete list on its site) gives every personal credit card: the Classic, TOP, Mais Mola, Gold, Gold Prestige, Flamingo Classic, Flamingo Gold and Platinum/Flamingo Platinum cards cost 800, 350, 500, 1,650, 1,750, 1,000, 1,600 and 3,600 meticais a year, are issued free (an urgent issue costs 550, on request only, not written), and charge 3% a month (2.5% for Mais Mola), written monthly as the list gives it first; the holder may pay 10% to 100% of the balance, so the minimum is 10%. The column headings of the complete list's credit card table were read by eye. The card the file called 'Cartão de Crédito' before is the Classic, renamed. The 2% default interest the list applies to every overdue instalment of a credit operation isn't written, as it doesn't say whether it is a monthly or yearly rate on the card. The business cards aren't written. Wave 4 (30 October 2026), for a second and third bank: BCI's price list page answered a captcha and Standard Bank Moçambique's site a Cloudflare 403; Absa Moçambique's site links no price list and Moza Banco's and FNB Moçambique's didn't answer usefully. Access Bank Moçambique, the next issuer a search found publishing a current complete price list, was added: its preçário completo (in force from 29 June 2026), read for its personal credit cards: the Classic, Gold and Platinum Particular cards cost 714, 918 and 1,122 meticais to issue (an urgent issue costs more, on request only, not written) and the same each year, charge 4% a month (48% a year; written monthly, as the list gives it first), and 244.80 meticais for a cash advance at an ATM, at home or abroad. Its prices include 2% stamp duty, so no tax is added. The 2% charge for late payment doesn't say 2% of what, so it isn't written; the 510-metical charge for changing the credit limit is a fixed sum at a raise, which the form can't carry, so it isn't written. The Empresa cards are business cards and aren't written.
